steps.label: Claim: a classical simulation could skip logging which-path data
In a classical simulation, each particle has a definite path anyway
steps.sub: Whether or not that fact gets written to a log

steps.label: Interference needs no definite path to exist at all
steps.sub: Not 'unlogged' — genuinely absent from the underlying model

steps.label: You can't recover interference from bookkeeping choices
steps.sub: On top of a model that already has definite single-path trajectories

steps.label: "Why only exactly 0 or 1, never in between?"
steps.sub: Postulates 2 & 3 — Hermitian operators have eigenvalues 0 and 1, and outcomes are always one of them

steps.label: "Why only a probability beforehand, not the outcome?"
steps.sub: Postulate 3 — the Born rule is the most QM promises about one trial

steps.label: "Why the same result on an immediate re-measurement?"
steps.sub: Postulate 4 — the first measurement already collapsed the state

steps.label: Blackbody radiation, the photoelectric effect, spectral lines
steps.sub: All three are the same fact — energy isn't continuously divisible — in three settings

steps.label: "No hydrogen atom means it's not real QM" — false
steps.sub: The five postulates ARE the theory; the hydrogen atom is just one application of it

steps.label: Skipping an application isn't skipping the theory
steps.sub: Circuits only ever need postulate 1 (the state) and postulate 5 (unitary gates)

subtitle: Building the qubit itself on top of exactly this foundation.
